Maya: Quick sync — after yesterday's ingest-enrich rollout we're seeing p99 latency spikes on the enrichment path for large envelopes, and cost for that route jumped ~22% in the last 6h. Anyone else see this?
Jon S: Yep saw the same in traces. p50 ok, tail exploded. Looks like many small fetches per envelope.
Priya K: Can you paste an example envelope size? I can run the enrichment harness locally.
Maya: Example envelope where it spikes: ~750KB payload with ~120 attributes. Repro attached (link to gist). :link:
Sam R: My initial theory: callers are invoking fetchEnrichment(key) inside a loop rather than using the batch API, causing N network ops. Where is the interface surface for that?
Jon S: Interface is in ingest-enrich v2: fetchEnrichments(keys: string[]): Map<string,Enrichment>. We added the batch API a while back but some legacy callers still call fetchEnrichment(key) one-at-a-time.
Priya K: Two possible remediation paths: 1) fix callers to call batch; 2) make runtime auto-batch single-key calls into micro-batches (N=32/64). Tradeoffs?
Maya: Auto-batching reduces network overhead but increases peak mem and can add head-of-line delay for small envelopes. Fixing callers is safest but slow.
Sam R: Operational suggestion: add a lint rule to detect looped single-key fetches at compile time + a runtime telemetry counter to surface single-vs-batch call ratios.
observability-bot: FYI — canary deployment window for ingest-enrich v2 scheduled 2026-03-24 02:00 UTC (rolling).
Jon S: Another angle: cost attribution. Today we attribute cost at ingest/envelope level but enrichment calls incur separate cost and aren't surfaced on envelope dashboards. That hides the true per-envelope unit cost.
Priya K: Proposal: emit an enrich_cost metric (enrich.cost_usd) as a micro-metric tagged with billing_key, enrichment_cohort, and envelope_id, and attach it to the trace/span so aggregators can roll up by tenant or cohort.
Sam R: Be careful with envelope_id as a tag — high cardinality. Aggregator should never index by envelope_id; it's for join-window only. Use billing_key + enrichment_cohort as rollup dimensions.
Maya: Implementation detail: add a span (kind=client) for enrichment calls, set attribute enrich.cost_usd (stringified float) and enrich.batch_size, and emit a lightweight counter metric with billing_key + enrichment_cohort.
Jon S: For aggregator side, we can sum enrich.cost_usd per billing_key over 1h windows and stitch to envelope counts. We also need to handle sampling — if traces are sampled, enrich metrics still need deterministic scaling.
Priya K: Plan for rollout: 1) emit enrich.cost_usd in canary but do not index it; 2) sample 1% of traffic for full trace attributes for 24h; 3) increase to 10% if signal stable; 4) enable indexed rollups by billing_key once we validate cardinality.
Sam R: For immediate mitigation, I'll prototype a micro-batching layer in the runtime that groups single-key fetches arriving within 5ms windows to the batch API (configurable). That should reduce network ops quickly.
Maya: Nice. Action items: Priya -> PR to update top 10 callers to batch API and test harness. Sam -> lint rule + runtime micro-batching prototype. Jon -> update observability docs on new enrich.* metrics and aggregator behavior. I'll own the rollout doc + canary plan.
Priya K: I'll also open an infra ticket for temporary extra capacity during canary (to avoid autoscaler noise).
Sam R: Noted. Will post a draft PR link when ready.
Maya: Thanks team. Meeting to follow-up Friday 10:00am PST to review canary results. :calendar:
